headline: Diesel prices near record highs as Ukraine strikes hit more Russian refineries
intro: Diesel just keeps grinding higher — retail's flirting with $5.65 and crack spreads north of $100/bbl — while Washington's biofuel exemption plans threaten to pour gasoline on the fire.
overview: Diesel cracks are blowing out (over $104/bbl) as Ukrainian drone strikes continue to knock Russian refining capacity offline, pushing US retail diesel toward all-time highs near $5.65/gal even as crude softens on Iran de-escalation hopes. Meanwhile, reports that EPA could grant sweeping small-refinery RFS exemptions are drawing fierce pushback from biodiesel and soybean groups warning of lost demand and higher diesel prices, and refiners face an added crude-supply squeeze as Canadian oil sands output falls and Asian buyers scoop up US barrels.

decks.title: 10-Q (filed 2026-08-25)
decks.analysis:
## Fuel-Segment Extract: BJ's Wholesale Club 10-Q (Q2 FY2026, period ended Aug 1, 2026)

- **Station count:** 206 gas stations across 22 states as of August 1, 2026 (down from BJ's operating alongside 267 clubs; company had 255 clubs a year ago, implying net club growth but gas station count not broken out historically in this filing).
- **Gasoline sales mix rising sharply:** "Gasoline and Other" grew to **25% of net sales in Q2 FY26** (vs. 18% in Q2 FY25) and **23% for the 26-week period** (vs. 18% prior year) — the largest categorical mix shift in the disclosure.
- **Gasoline comparable sales:** **+8.8%** for the thirteen weeks and **+6.9%** for the twenty-six weeks ended Aug 1, 2026, driven by both **higher average retail price-per-gallon** and **increased comparable gallons sold** — no absolute gallon figures disclosed.
- **Margin strategy:** Company states it "generally attempt[s] to maintain a fairly stable gross profit per gallon on an absolute dollar basis," so rising retail pump prices lift net sales dollars but are framed as largely margin-neutral per-gallon; volatile crude/wholesale swings cause temporary "margin contraction or expansion" versus competitors depending on procurement timing.
- **Membership-fuel linkage/rewards economics:** Club+ members get a **5¢/gallon** discount at BJ's Gas; BJ's One/One+ co-branded Mastercard holders get up to a **15¢/gallon** discount when paying at BJ's gas locations — reinforcing fuel as a membership-retention lever tied to card royalty/rewards revenue (recognized via royalty revenue and co-brand deferred revenue balances in Note 3).
- **Cost structure:** "Other segment expenses" (which include gasoline cost of revenue) rose from $911.5M to $1.43B YoY in the quarter and from $1.79B to $2.61B YoY for the half, consistent with higher wholesale fuel costs flowing through cost of sales alongside higher retail pump prices.

**Signal for fuels markets:** BJ's data point to firmer retail pump prices and higher fuel volumes through mid-2026 versus the prior-year period, with the retailer maintaining stable per-gallon dollar margins — indicating resilient consumer fuel demand at warehouse-club price points rather than a margin-driven earnings story.
